task:
DO NOT CALL ANY TOOLS. Review this proposed SummonScout 1.82 patch and return APPROVE or BLOCK with concrete reasons. This is the final pre-merge review.

PATCH A FleetChatBurstGuard v2: FCV remains 12s presence. C.capability is wrapped so every FCV no longer sends FCE. It queues first-seen peers, otherwise only when age since last FCE >= KEEPALIVE=28s. C.broadcast no longer sends; it clears globalHash so next 0.25s tick detects state change. payloadHash = active|price|rosterCsv|freshServices. On hash change, all fresh peers are queued staggered by SEND_GAP=4.5s. queueKeepalives scans fresh C.peers and queues peers with lastSent nil or age>=28s, likewise staggered. drain sends at most one baseCapability and enforces 4.5s global gap; lastSent stamped only after successful baseCapability. Legacy H/D remains suppressed. Startup grace 3s. R/X/A and advert traffic untouched.

PATCH B LocalDestinationInviteGuard v3: hard safety semantics unchanged. Before base invite, slave-safety/disabled still returns false,'slave-safety-blocked'; wrong service still false,'wrong-service-hard-guard'. After base, any false reason except duplicate-event is recorded. On rejection only, provider sends one bounded/sanitized `[SSI ROUTEFAIL] provider -> customer / dest / reason / ready= / enabled= / service=` whisper to configured master (not to itself), stores W112_SUMMONSCOUT_ROUTE_LAST_FAILURE. Customer-facing unavailable remains generic. No InviteByName added.

TOC 1.82; static test asserts load order, 4.5s/28s cadence, hard guard strings, no R/X/A or InviteByName in burst/guard modules.

Review for Lua 5.0 correctness, TTL/cadence correctness with 4-5 peers, accidental repeated queueing, state-change storms, wrapper recursion, security/spam regressions, and whether ROUTEFAIL can itself meaningfully recreate idle spam. If a fix is required, give the minimal exact change. Under 700 words.
